chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Mu'awiyah ibn Wahb, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

The deceased is shrouded in five garments: a qamis that is not buttoned upon him, an izar, a cloth with which his middle is bound, a burd in which he is wrapped, and a turban with which he is turbaned, and its excess is cast over his face.
As for the cotton, we shall mention it when explaining the washing and the embalming, if Allah, Exalted is He, wills.

Then he said, may Allah, Exalted is He, support him: Let two fresh palm stalks be prepared, green, and the length of each one of them should be the measure of the forearm bone. If palm stalks are not found, they are substituted with khilaf; if khilaf is not found, they are substituted with sidr; if none of these trees is found and another kind of tree is found, it is substituted for them, provided that it is fresh. If none of that is found, then there is no hardship upon a person in leaving it due to necessity.

key_terms.جَرِيدَتَانِ: two fresh stalks prepared for the burial rite
key_terms.خَمْسَةِ أَثْوَابٍ: five garments used for the kafan
key_terms.خِرْقَةٍ: a cloth used to bind the middle of the deceased
key_terms.عِمَامَةٍ: a turban used as part of the shrouding
key_terms.قَمِيصٍ: a shirt-like garment used in the shroud
key_terms.لِلِاضْطِرَارِ: due to necessity; indicating concession in case of inability
key_terms.يُكَفَّنُ: is shrouded; refers to the prescribed enshrouding of the deceased

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the shrouding of the deceased and the use of fresh stalks in burial rites?
ai.summary: This report outlines legal rulings concerning the kafan of the deceased, specifying five garments and mentioning the preparation of two fresh stalks to accompany the burial rites. It also establishes substitute materials when the preferred types are unavailable, and lifts hardship when necessity prevents fulfilling this practice.
